title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Solicitation Assembly - Specifications
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which type of specification focuses on the required outcome or the intended use of a product, allowing vendors the flexibility to propose their own technical solutions?
questions.explain: A performance specification describes what the product or service is expected to do (its function and outcome) rather than how it must be built, encouraging innovation and wider competition.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When an agency uses a 'Brand Name or Equal' specification, what must the buyer prominently include in the solicitation document to ensure fair competition?
options: A mandatory requirement that only the brand name manufacturer can bid
The salient characteristics and essential features that an 'equal' product must meet
A waiver of the public bid opening requirement
questions.explain: To allow vendors to offer 'equal' alternatives, the solicitation must clearly list the salient physical, functional, or performance characteristics of the brand name item that must be met.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A requesting department submits a specification for a fleet of trucks that lists engine dimensions exact to the millimeter. Only one manufacturer makes this exact engine. The specification is considered:
questions.explain: Specifications that unnecessarily restrict competition to a single vendor, without a valid operational or safety justification, violate public procurement principles of full and open competition.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a Scope of Work (SOW) and a Statement of Work (SOW) in standard procurement terminology?
options: There is no difference; they are interchangeable terms
A Scope of Work broadly defines the high-level goals and limits of a project, while a Statement of Work provides detailed, specific tasks and deliverables required
A Scope of Work is used for goods, while a Statement of Work is used strictly for services
A Scope of Work is written by the vendor, while a Statement of Work is written by the buyer
questions.explain: While often used interchangeably in practice, formally, a Scope of Work is a high-level description of boundaries and objectives. A Statement of Work details the specific tasks, timelines, deliverables, and performance standards required.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A specification requires a material to withstand temperatures of 500 degrees Fahrenheit, +/- 5 degrees. The '+/- 5 degrees' is known as a:
questions.explain: A tolerance is the allowable variation from a specified standard or measurement in a specification. It provides acceptable boundaries for physical or performance characteristics.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency repeatedly purchases a highly specific grade of safety equipment. To streamline future bidding, the procurement office pre-tests various manufacturers' items and creates a list of approved products. This is known as a:
questions.explain: A Qualified Products List (QPL) identifies products that have been tested and approved in advance of a solicitation, allowing only those pre-approved products to be bid on future contracts.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: If a design specification is used, who typically assumes the risk if the final product is manufactured exactly to specification but fails to perform the intended function?
options: The manufacturer of the raw materials
questions.explain: Under the Spearin Doctrine, if an agency issues a detailed design specification, there is an implied warranty that the design is adequate. Therefore, the agency assumes the risk if the design fails to produce the desired result, provided the vendor followed it perfectly.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: To ensure maximum competition and obtain the most current technological solutions, an agency should draft specifications based heavily on:
options: Thorough market research and industry standards
The specific preferences of the department's longest-tenured employee
questions.explain: Market research allows buyers to understand current commercial capabilities, standard industry practices, and innovations, ensuring specifications are modern, non-restrictive, and highly competitive.
